main_diagnosis: The simulator shows a large model-data mismatch (high negative log-marginal NLE). Two primary problems likely cause this: (1) the second extra channel slot (X2) is not used while both flexible params are consumed by X1, reducing model flexibility; (2) the model lacks a subthreshold depolarizing current (persistent Na / NaP) and uses overly permissive parameter ranges (V_half mapping, noise and conductance caps), which together make it hard to reproduce tonic, subthreshold-driven spiking without producing unrealistic behavior.

issues.description: Flexible parameter allocation and channel slots are inconsistent: both flexible params (params[:,8:10]) are mapped to X1 (V_half_p and tau_base_p) while X2 is left unused (gbar_X2 is present but has no associated flexible parameters). This wastes model capacity and violates the stated two-parameter-per-slot design, limiting the simulator's ability to capture missing subthreshold dynamics.
issues.location: DiscoveredSimulator.forward: parameter extraction and mapping (near lines where gbar_X1 = params[:,6], gbar_X2 = params[:,7], param_i_pos = params[:,8], param_j_pos = params[:,9], and X1 design block)
issues.suggestion: Reallocate the parameter vector so each extra slot (X1, X2) receives two tunable parameters. For example: use params[:,6] = gbar_X1, params[:,7] = X1_param (e.g. V_half or tau), params[:,8] = gbar_X2, params[:,9] = X2_param. Then implement X2 dynamics using its own two parameters. If you want X1 to keep two parameters, expand the parameter vector or reassign such that X1 and X2 each get exactly two tunable params. Update initializations, gating and the mapping comments accordingly. This restores the intended capacity of two pre-allocated channels and enables testing a second mechanism (e.g. NaP) without overloading X1.

issues.description: Missing a subthreshold inward conductance and overly-broad parameter ranges degrade fit to tonic spiking data. The current single added M-type K+ is helpful to reduce excitability but cannot create the sustained subthreshold depolarization or fine ISI shaping that a small persistent Na (NaP) or a transient A-type K (I_A) can provide. Additionally, several clamps and mappings permit extreme values (V_half mapped over [-150,150], nois_fact allowed up to 1e6, gbar maxima very large) that allow unrealistic regimes and make inference harder.
issues.location: DiscoveredSimulator.forward: X1 design block, parameter clamping and mapping (V_half_p mapping from param_i_pos and tau_base_p from param_j_pos), and noise/parameter clamps (nois_fact clamp, gbar_* clamps).
issues.suggestion: 1) Implement a small persistent sodium (NaP) in X2 (or repurpose X2) to provide a subthreshold inward drive that supports tonic firing without bursting. Implementation notes: - Use gbar_X2 (tunable) and a second tunable parameter for V_half_NaP (or slope). - Model NaP as non-inactivating (instantaneous m_inf or fast tau), e.g. m_inf = 1/(1+exp(-(V - V_half_NaP)/k)), g_NaP_eff = gbar_X2 * m_inf, and add I_NaP_term = g_NaP_eff * E_Na in the V_inf numerator and g_NaP_eff in g_tot. - Keep NaP small (start with gbar_X2 up to a few mS/cm^2) and V_half_NaP in a subthreshold window (recommend clamp to roughly [-70, -40] mV) so it increases excitability without producing sustained HF or bursting. 2) Tighten parameter ranges to physiologically plausible windows: - Reduce V_half_p mapping range from [-150,150] to something like [-100,-20] mV (or narrower based on data). - Cap nois_fact to a much smaller maximum (e.g. <= 50) to prevent extreme stochastic excursions. - Lower max gbar_X1/gbar_X2 to e.g. 200 mS/cm^2 or a dataset-informed bound. 3) Optionally allow NaP to be instantaneous (no dynamic gating) to keep parsimony; if a dynamic gate is used give it a small tau (1–20 ms). These changes will (a) increase the model's ability to recreate subthreshold depolarization that leads to tonic spiking, (b) avoid bursting-prone kinetics, and (c) reduce pathological parameter regimes that inflate the evidence penalty.
